newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scor falls on report it may lose contract.
newsitem.headline: Scor falls on report it may lose contract.

text.p: Shares in re-insurance company Scor were down more than three percent on Friday on the bourse, which was trading at year highs, on a report that it may lose a big re-insurance contract from a merged Axa-UAP entity, brokers said.
"The new Axa/UAP would not long re-insure 'big risks' through Scor, but would turn to Munich Re or Jardine, which have more competitive rates," the weekly La Vie Francaise said.
Scor shares were down 5.20 francs at 182.30 at 1100 GMT. The Paris bourse's CAC index was up 0.8 percent at 2,308.82 points.
Axa and UAP announced plans to merge a month ago.

"What we know is that UAP did not have Scor as its lead manager for major risks," said an Axa spokeswoman. "We are just trying to find out how much business Axa represents for Scor. But in any case, as in everything being discussed about what will happen after UAP merges with Scor, all of this talk is completely premature. No decision has been taken."
Scor could not immediately be reached for comment.
